newsitem.title: USA: JP Foodservice to buy Rykoff for $1.4 billion.
newsitem.headline: JP Foodservice to buy Rykoff for $1.4 billion.

text.p: JP Foodservice Inc. has agreed to acquire Rykoff-Sexton Inc. in a deal worth $1.4 billion in cash and debt, creating a food-service giant with annual sales of $5.2 billion, the companies said on Monday.
Together, the companies will have nationwide distribution capabilities and a customer base of more than 130,000 hotel, restaurant and institutional foodservice customers.

Rykoff shareholders will receive 0.84 JP share for each Rykoff share in a tax-free transaction. The exchange ratio will not change if JP's stock price changes, the companies said in a news release. It is expected that JP and Rykoff shareholders will own equal stakes in the combined company.
JP's and Rykoff's shares, which closed Friday at $30.125 and $19.625 respectively on the New York Stock Exchange, did not trade early Monday.
The deal, in which JP will assume $700 million of Rykoff debt, is expected to be accretive to JP's earnings in 1998 and thereafter, the companies said.

JP Chairman/Chief Executive Jim Miller will be chairman/chief executive of the new company, while Rykoff Chairman/Chief Executive Mark Van Stekelenburg will be vice chairman and president. The merged companies will be called JP Foodservice Inc; its operating units will do business as US Foodservice.
The deal is subject to shareholder and regulatory approval. Headquarters of the new company will be in Columbia, Md., the current home of JP. Rykoff is based in Wilkes-Barre, Pa.
